I've been farming this land for 20 years. I know what works here in Quzhou — the soil, the market buyers, the dry spells between rain. My wife and I manage everything ourselves now, so I plan around what two people can handle.

My main rotation is the same as always: spring cabbage, then Chinese cabbage in summer, then autumn cabbage on the same 4 mu. That land stays busy all year and I know how to read it. The other 2 mu I split — 1 mu chili, 1 mu kidney bean. Chili brings good cash when the price is right, and kidney bean I've been growing since my father's time.

I buy hybrid seeds for cabbage and Chinese cabbage from the county supply store. The market buyers want uniform heads — saved seeds don't give me that anymore. For kidney bean I still use my own saved seeds from last year's best pods. For chili I use an improved variety I've been buying for the past 5 years — better disease resistance in this heat.

Fertilizer I apply the same way I always have: base fertilizer before planting (mostly diammonium phosphate), then urea top-dress when the plants are establishing and again at heading for cabbage. Chili I'm careful not to overfeed early or I get too much leaf and not enough fruit. Kidney bean fixes its own nitrogen so I go light on urea there.

Irrigation from my well — I check the soil by hand. Cabbage I water about 4 times a season. Chili in summer heat needs more. Kidney bean is more tolerant of dry spells so I irrigate less.

Pesticides — I spray when I see the problem, not on a fixed schedule. Cabbage gets caterpillars and aphids. Chili gets aphids bad and sometimes mites in July. I use what the pesticide shop recommends for each pest.
